comments.content: `sourceLanguage` is declared optional on `Request` (`@JsonProperty(required = false)`, "default is zh"), but `apply` now rejects the request when it is blank. The only place `"zh"` is defaulted is the single-argument convenience constructor, which Jackson does not use — Spring AI deserializes tool-call arguments through the canonical 3-arg constructor. So any LLM tool call that omits `sourceLanguage` (the documented optional case) hits `return null` instead of translating, which is a regression versus the previous hardcoded `LANGUAGE_CODE` behaviour. Normalize the missing value instead of rejecting it.

Since `setPropertiesFromEnv` silently picks them up, credentials exported for a completely different tool in the same environment would be used here, producing hard-to-diagnose auth failures. comments.content: `response.get()` can throw `InterruptedException`, but the broad `catch (Exception)` swallows it without restoring the interrupt flag, so an interrupted tool-execution thread keeps running with a cleared interrupt status. In addition, logging only `e.getMessage()` drops the stack trace (e.g. for `ExecutionException`/NPE), making failures hard to diagnose. Handle `InterruptedException` separately (re-interrupt) and log the throwable.
